newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says it assumes its soldier was kidnapped.
newsitem.headline: Israel says it assumes its soldier was kidnapped.

text.p: Israel's defence minister said on Monday security forces now assumed a soldier who went missing in Israel in September was kidnapped.
Sharon Edri, 19, was last seen on September 11 at a medical clinic at an army base in central Israel.

"As long as we have no other evidence, from our point of view Sharon Edri is being held against his will somewhere and we are making every effort in order to find him," Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai told Israel's army radio on Monday.

A subsequent statement from Police Commissioner Assaf Hefetz said: "The police didn't exclude since the beginning any option and now we tend to give more weight or attention to the kidnapping option."

A police spokeswoman declined to say if Edri might have been kidnapped by criminals or Arab militants. Searches were conducted in a wooded area near the family home outside Jerusalem following his disappearance.
Arab militants have kidnapped Israeli soldiers in Israel in the past but issued claims of responsibility, along with demands, not long after seizing them.

In the last such incident, Nachshon Wachsman was kidnapped by the Islamic Hamas group militants in October 1994 and killed during a shootout between Israeli commandos trying to free him and his Hamas kidnappers at a hideout in the West Bank.
